heading: January 2025: transition week actions
body:
In the days before his second inauguration Trump moved on several fronts at once.[n] On January 16, 2025 he named Mel Gibson, Sylvester Stallone and Jon Voight as [[hollywood-special-ambassadors|Hollywood special ambassadors]] to serve as his "eyes and ears" in the entertainment capital, saying the goal was bringing back business lost to foreign countries.[n] He said he would use the momentum of the freshly agreed Gaza ceasefire to expand the [[abraham-accords|Abraham Accords]], writing on [[truth-social|Truth Social]] that his national security team, through Special Envoy to the Middle East [[steve-witkoff|Steve Witkoff]], would work with Israel and allies to ensure Gaza "NEVER again becomes a terrorist safe haven" while continuing to promote "PEACE THROUGH STRENGTH."[n] Having repeatedly threatened "hell to pay" if hostages were not released before his January 20 inauguration, he said he was "thrilled American and Israeli hostages will be returning home."[n] In a podcast interview with [[dan-bongino|Dan Bongino]] he said of the deal, "We changed the course of it, and we changed it fast, and frankly, it better be done before I take the oath of office," adding, "We shook hands, and we signed certain documents, but it better be done."[n] Trump also personally encouraged [[vivek-ramaswamy|Vivek Ramaswamy]] to accept appointment to Ohio's vacant Senate seat if offered.[n]

Reporting at the time characterized "Trump 2.0" as a radically different and potentially more potent figure than the one who arrived in Washington eight years earlier, better versed in how Washington works, backed by a disciplined operation under chief of staff [[susie-wiles|Susie Wiles]], holding the full support of the Republican Party and a popular-vote mandate.[n] Badlands contributor Burning Bright cast Trump as "the James T. Kirk of the Info War and the Shadow War," with the Middle East as his [[kobayashi-maru|Kobayashi Maru]] — an apparently unwinnable test whose parameters he intends to rewrite rather than accept.[n]
